easy.def: A small, round, green vegetable.
examples: I eat peas.
The pea is green.
Peas grow in a pod.

more.def: A small, round, green seed that grows in a pod and is eaten as a vegetable.
examples: I ate peas with my dinner.
Peas grow in a long pod.
She rolled a pea across her plate.

easy.def: A time without fighting.
examples: The countries live in peace.
Peace came at last.
We wish for peace.

more.def: A time when there is no war or fighting.
examples: The two countries signed a treaty of peace.
People marched for peace.
After years of war, peace came.

easy.def: Being calm and quiet.
examples: I like peace and quiet.
The lake was full of peace.
Leave me in peace.

more.def: A calm, quiet feeling or place.
examples: I enjoy the peace of the forest.
The baby slept in peace.
He read in peace on the porch.

easy.def: Calm and quiet.
examples: The garden is a peaceful place.
The baby looks peaceful when asleep.
We had a peaceful day at the lake.

more.def: Quiet and calm; without fighting or trouble.
examples: It was a peaceful morning with no sound but the birds.
The two countries found a peaceful way to solve their problem.
The village is peaceful at night.

easy.def: In a calm and quiet way.
examples: The baby slept peacefully.
The lake lay peacefully still.
We played peacefully.

more.def: In a calm, quiet way, without any fighting or noise.
examples: The baby slept peacefully through the whole car ride.
Cows grazed peacefully on the green hill.
The two countries lived peacefully side by side for many years.

easy.def: A soft, juicy fruit with a fuzzy skin.
examples: I eat a peach.
The peach is sweet.
A peach has a pit.

more.def: A round, juicy fruit with soft yellow-orange flesh and fuzzy skin.
examples: I ate a ripe peach for a snack.
Juice dripped from the peach.
The peach tree is full of fruit.

easy.def: The pointed top of a mountain.
examples: We climbed to the peak.
The peak is snowy.
The mountain has two peaks.

more.def: The highest point of a mountain, or the highest point of anything.
examples: The hikers reached the peak at noon.
The snowy peak shone in the sun.
The crowd was at its peak at noon.

easy.def: A small nut that grows underground.
examples: I like peanut butter.
The peanut is small.
The squirrel ate a peanut.

more.def: A small, round seed in a thin shell that grows under the ground and is eaten as a snack.
examples: I had a peanut butter sandwich.
Peanuts grow under the ground.
The elephant took a peanut with its trunk.

easy.def: A poor farm worker in the past.
examples: The peasant worked in the field.
Peasants lived in small huts.
The peasant grew wheat.

more.def: A poor person who worked on the land in the past, often for a lord.
examples: The peasant worked the field from dawn to dusk.
Long ago, peasants grew wheat for the lord.
The peasant lived in a small hut.

easy.def: Strange or odd.
examples: That is a peculiar hat!
The soup has a peculiar taste.
My cat makes a peculiar sound.

more.def: Strange or unusual in a way that makes you notice.
examples: There was a peculiar smell coming from the science room.
It was peculiar that the shop was closed on a Monday.
The bird had a peculiar way of hopping sideways.

easy.def: To look quickly or secretly.
examples: I peek at the gift.
She peeked out the window.
Do not peek.

more.def: To take a quick, sneaky look at something.
examples: I peeked at my birthday gift.
The cat peeked through the fence.
The child peeked around the corner.

easy.def: To take the skin off.
examples: I peel a banana.
She peeled the apple.
Peel the orange.

more.def: To remove the outer skin of a fruit or vegetable.
examples: I peeled the banana.
She peeled the apples for the pie.
Dad peeled the potatoes.

easy.def: The skin of a fruit.
examples: The banana peel is yellow.
I threw away the peel.
An orange peel smells sweet.

more.def: The thin outer skin of a fruit or vegetable.
examples: She saved the lemon peel for the cake.
I slipped on a banana peel in the cartoon.
She grated lemon peel into the cake.

easy.def: To look quickly or secretly.
examples: I peep out the window.
She peeped around the door.
The child peeped.

more.def: To look quickly or in secret through a small opening.
examples: I peeped out the window to see the snow.
She peeped around the door at the surprise.
The kitten peeped from the box.

easy.def: A tiny, high sound.
examples: The chick made a peep.
I heard a peep.
Not a peep was heard.

more.def: A very small, high sound like a young bird makes.
examples: The chick gave a tiny peep.
I did not hear a peep from the baby.
Not a peep came from the nest.

easy.def: A person who is your age or in your group.
examples: She plays with her peers.
Kids learn from their peers.
My peers are my classmates.

more.def: A person who is the same age or in the same group as you.
examples: She plays with her peers on the playground.
Kids often learn from their peers.
Her peers voted her class president.

easy.def: To look closely at something.
examples: I peer through the window.
She peered at the map.
He peered into the hole.

more.def: To look hard at something, often because it is hard to see.
examples: I peered through the window to see who was there.
She peered at the tiny writing on the map.
He peered into the dark cave.

easy.def: A thing you use to write with.
examples: I write with a blue pen.
My pen ran out of ink.
Please lend me a pen.

more.def: A tool with ink inside that you use to write or draw.
examples: She signed her name with a black pen.
The teacher marked our papers with a red pen.
I always keep a pen in my backpack.

easy.def: A small fenced place for animals.
examples: The pigs are in the pen.
The farmer put the sheep in a pen.
We built a pen for the rabbits.

more.def: A small area with a fence around it, used to keep animals in.
examples: The farmer fed the pigs in their pen.
A gate kept the lambs safe inside the pen.
We cleaned the pen where the baby goats sleep.

easy.def: A punishment for breaking a rule.
examples: The penalty was a fine.
The team got a penalty.
The penalty is five minutes.

more.def: A punishment or loss that you get for breaking a rule.
examples: The penalty for being late is a fine.
The player got a penalty for pushing.
The team scored on a penalty kick.

easy.def: A thin stick you write with.
examples: I write with a pencil.
The pencil is sharp.
I lost my pencil.

more.def: A thin tool for writing or drawing, with a center of lead or color.
examples: I wrote my name with a pencil.
She sharpened her pencil.
The teacher gave out new pencils.

easy.def: To go into or through something.
examples: The sun can penetrate the clouds.
A nail can penetrate wood.
Water penetrated my boots.

more.def: To pass into or through something, often something thick or hard to get through.
examples: Sunlight could not penetrate the thick leaves of the forest.
The cold wind penetrated her thin coat.
A sharp needle penetrated the cloth with ease.

easy.def: A black and white bird that swims and cannot fly.
examples: The penguin swims fast.
We saw a penguin at the zoo.
A penguin waddled on the ice.

more.def: A black and white sea bird that cannot fly but swims very well, found in cold places.
examples: A penguin slid on its belly across the ice.
Penguins huddle together to keep warm in the freezing wind.
The penguin dove into the sea to catch a fish.

easy.def: A small coin worth one cent.
examples: I found a penny on the ground.
She put a penny in the jar.
A penny is brown.

more.def: A coin worth one cent, which is one hundredth of a dollar.
examples: Abraham Lincoln's face is on the penny.
He saved every penny to buy the kite.
A hundred pennies make one dollar.

easy.def: Men, women, and children.
examples: Many people came.
The people clapped.
Some people like cats.

more.def: More than one person, or all the men, women, and children of a place or group.
examples: A lot of people were waiting in line at the museum.
The people of the village built a new school together.
People all over the world celebrate the new year.

easy.def: Lots of energy and good spirits.
examples: She has lots of pep.
A pep talk gave us energy.
I have no pep today.

more.def: Lively energy and cheerfulness.
examples: She has lots of pep and never gets tired.
The coach gave a pep talk before the game.
The band played with great pep.

easy.def: A spice that makes food taste hot.
examples: I put pepper on my eggs.
The pepper is black.
Pass the pepper.

more.def: A hot-tasting powder made from dried berries, used to flavor food.
examples: Dad shook pepper on the potatoes.
The pepper made me sneeze.
Salt and pepper are on the table.

easy.def: A hollow vegetable that can be red, green or yellow.
examples: I like bell peppers.
The pepper is red.
She sliced a pepper.

more.def: A hollow, colorful vegetable that is eaten raw or cooked.
examples: We added red peppers to the salad.
The green pepper was crisp.
She stuffed the pepper with rice.

easy.def: For each.
examples: The apples cost two dollars per bag.
The speed limit is thirty miles per hour.
I eat three meals per day.

more.def: For each one, or in each.
examples: The bus goes forty miles per hour.
The apples cost two dollars per pound.
Each student gets two pencils per week.

easy.def: To notice something with your senses or mind.
examples: I perceive a sound.
She perceives a change.
We perceive light with our eyes.

more.def: To become aware of something through your senses or mind.
examples: I perceive a sound in the dark.
She perceived a change in the weather.
We perceive light with our eyes and sound with our ears.

easy.def: A part of one hundred.
examples: Fifty percent is half.
I got ninety percent on the test.
Ten percent of the class is absent.

more.def: One part in every hundred, written with the sign %.
examples: Half of the class is fifty percent.
She got ninety percent of the answers right.
The store took twenty percent off the price of the shirt.

easy.def: A part of something, written out of one hundred.
examples: A large percentage of the class came.
The percentage is fifty.
What percentage did you get?

more.def: An amount shown as a number of parts out of every hundred.
examples: A large percentage of the class has a pet.
I got a high percentage of the answers right on the test.
What percentage of the pizza did you eat?

easy.def: Having nothing wrong.
examples: The weather is perfect.
Her drawing is perfect.
It was a perfect day.

more.def: As good as it can be, with no mistakes or problems.
examples: The weather was perfect for a picnic.
She got a perfect score on the spelling test.
This hat is a perfect fit.

easy.def: Being perfect.
examples: The cake was baked to perfection.
She aims for perfection.
The song was played to perfection.

more.def: The state of being without any fault or mistake.
examples: She polished the speech to perfection.
She practiced until she reached perfection.
The dancers moved with perfection.

easy.def: In a way that is just right.
examples: She sang perfectly.
It fits perfectly.
The cake is perfectly round.

more.def: In a way that has no mistakes or flaws.
examples: She sang the song perfectly.
The key fits the lock perfectly.
The cake was perfectly round.

easy.def: To do something in front of people.
examples: The band will perform.
She performed a song.
They perform a play.

more.def: To do something, such as sing, dance or act, in front of an audience.
examples: The band will perform on Friday.
She performed a song for the class.
The students performed a play.

easy.def: To do a job or task.
examples: The machine performs well.
The doctor performed surgery.
She performs the task.

more.def: To do a job or a piece of work.
examples: The machine performs its job well.
The doctor performed the operation.
The robot performs simple tasks.

easy.def: A show for an audience.
examples: The dance performance was fun.
We went to a performance.
Her performance was great.

more.def: A show in which people sing, act, dance or play music for others.
examples: The school held a performance of the spring play.
The band's performance made everyone clap.
The dancers practiced for weeks before the performance.

easy.def: A person who sings, dances or acts for an audience.
examples: The performer sang a song.
A performer juggled.
The performers took a bow.

more.def: A person who sings, dances, acts or does tricks in front of an audience.
examples: The performer sang a song for the crowd.
A circus performer juggled five balls.
The performers took a bow when the show was over.

easy.def: A liquid with a nice smell that people put on.
examples: Mom wears perfume.
The perfume smells like roses.
The bottle of perfume is small.

more.def: A liquid with a sweet smell that people put on their skin.
examples: The perfume smelled like flowers.
She dabbed perfume on her wrist.
The bottle of perfume was shaped like a heart.

easy.def: Maybe.
examples: Perhaps it will rain.
Perhaps we can go later.
Perhaps she forgot.

more.def: Possibly; it may be so.
examples: Perhaps we could take a walk after dinner.
The package is late, perhaps because of the snow.
Perhaps the birds left because it got too cold.

easy.def: The distance around the edge of a shape.
examples: The perimeter of the square is eight.
Measure the perimeter.
The perimeter is the outside.

more.def: The total distance around the outside of a shape.
examples: The perimeter of the square is eight inches.
We measured the perimeter of the garden.
The fence runs along the perimeter of the yard.

easy.def: A dot at the end of a sentence.
examples: Put a period at the end.
A period is a dot.
The sentence ends with a period.

more.def: A small dot used at the end of a sentence.
examples: Put a period at the end of the sentence.
A period shows where a sentence stops.
The teacher circled the missing period.

easy.def: A length of time.
examples: A long period of time.
The period before lunch.
It was a quiet period.

more.def: A length of time during which something happens.
examples: The ice age was a long period of cold weather.
Math is the first period of the day.
There was a quiet period after the storm.

easy.def: To die or be destroyed.
examples: The grass will perish without rain.
The flowers perished in the frost.
The ice will perish.

more.def: To die or be destroyed, often because of cold, lack of water or other harsh things.
examples: Plants perish without water.
The flowers perished in the first frost of winter.
Many animals perished when the river dried up.

easy.def: To brighten up or become more lively.
examples: The puppy perks up.
The cat's ears perked.
I perk up when I smell pancakes.

more.def: To become more lively or to lift up with interest.
examples: The puppy perked up when it heard its name.
The cat's ears perked at the sound.
I perked up when I smelled the pancakes.

easy.def: An extra good thing that comes with something.
examples: A perk is a free snack.
The perk was a free ticket.
Free cookies are a perk.

more.def: An extra benefit that you get along with something, like a job.
examples: A perk of the job is free lunch.
Getting to pick the music is a perk of being the leader.
The hotel had a perk of free breakfast.

easy.def: Staying the same for a very long time.
examples: The marker is permanent.
She has a permanent job.
The mark is permanent.

more.def: Lasting for a very long time, or forever.
examples: The ink is permanent and will not wash off.
He got a permanent job at the library.
The wall is a permanent part of the building.

easy.def: When someone says it is okay to do something.
examples: I have permission to go outside.
Ask for permission first.
Dad gave me permission to ride my bike.

more.def: An okay from someone that allows you to do something.
examples: You need a parent's permission to go on the field trip.
The pilot waited for permission to land.
She asked permission to borrow her sister's sweater.

easy.def: To let someone do something.
examples: The sign does not permit dogs.
The teacher will permit it.
We will not permit running.

more.def: To say that someone may do something, or to make something possible.
examples: The rules do not permit dogs in the pool.
The teacher permitted us to go outside.
Good weather will permit us to play outside.

easy.def: A paper that gives you permission.
examples: We need a permit to fish.
The permit is for parking.
He has a fishing permit.

more.def: An official paper that says you are allowed to do something.
examples: You need a permit to fish in the lake.
Dad bought a parking permit.
The builder showed the permit to the city.

easy.def: A man, woman, or child.
examples: Each person has a seat.
She is a kind person.
One person came.

more.def: A human being, such as a man, woman, or child.
examples: Each person in the class made a card.
He is a kind person who always shares.
The elevator holds up to ten people, but only one person got in.

easy.def: Belonging to just one person.
examples: This is my personal diary.
Do not read my personal note.
She keeps her personal things in a box.

more.def: Belonging to or about one particular person, and not shared with others.
examples: My diary is personal, so please do not read it.
He asked a very personal question.
Each camper has a personal locker.

easy.def: The way a person acts and feels that makes them different.
examples: She has a friendly personality.
My dog has a funny personality.
He has a big personality.

more.def: All the qualities that make a person different from other people.
examples: She has a friendly, outgoing personality.
My cat has a shy personality.
Each twin has a different personality.

easy.def: As one person; you yourself.
examples: I will do it personally.
Personally, I like pizza.
He thanked her personally.

more.def: In person; or as far as you yourself are concerned.
examples: I will thank her personally.
Personally, I think pizza is the best food.
The mayor greeted each guest personally.

easy.def: A way of looking at something.
examples: From my perspective, it is fair.
See it from her perspective.
Each person has a perspective.

more.def: A point of view, or a way of thinking about something.
examples: From my perspective, the rule is fair.
Try to see the problem from her perspective.
Each of the three friends had a different perspective.

easy.def: To get someone to agree by giving reasons.
examples: I persuaded Mom to say yes.
She persuaded him to come.
They persuaded the teacher.

more.def: To convince someone to do something by giving good reasons.
examples: I persuaded Mom to let us get a dog.
She persuaded her friend to join the team.
The ad tries to persuade you to buy the toy.

easy.def: A poison used to kill bugs that harm plants.
examples: The farmer used pesticide.
Pesticide can hurt bees.
Do not touch pesticide.

more.def: A chemical that kills insects and other small animals that harm crops.
examples: The farmer sprayed pesticide on the apple trees.
Some pesticides can also harm bees and fish, so they must be used carefully.
Washing fruit helps remove any pesticide left on the skin.

easy.def: An animal you keep at home.
examples: My pet is a cat.
Do you have a pet?
The dog is a good pet.

more.def: An animal that lives with people and is cared for by them.
examples: A hamster can be a good pet for a small apartment.
She feeds her pet fish every morning.
The class pet is a gentle guinea pig.

easy.def: To stroke an animal gently.
examples: I pet the dog.
She petted the cat.
Please pet the rabbit softly.

more.def: To touch an animal gently with your hand.
examples: The children petted the soft lambs at the farm.
He petted the horse's nose.
Cats purr when you pet them.

easy.def: A paper that many people sign to ask for a change.
examples: We signed a petition.
The petition asks for a new park.
The class made a petition.

more.def: A written request signed by many people that asks someone in charge to do something.
examples: We signed a petition asking for a new playground.
The class made a petition to keep the library open.
Hundreds of people put their names on the petition.

easy.def: Small and not important.
examples: It was a petty argument.
The petty problem was solved.
He got upset over petty things.

more.def: Small and not important, or mean about small things.
examples: They had a petty argument over a pencil.
Petty quarrels wasted their afternoon.
Do not waste time on petty problems.
